health.body: {"status":"ok","database":"ok",...} — served from the stored component rows; no new health rows are being written

failures: Stability criterion failed and stopped the run (exit 20): the write queue never recovers. finish.sh measured lock warnings growing 1 -> 3 inside its 120s window and reported 'STOP: lock warnings grew past two: early=1 late=3'. A manual re-run sampled 1 at t=40s, 3 at t=100s, 5 at t=160s, 7 at t=220s, 8 shortly after - one write_queue_task_failed every 30s (the sqlite_busy_timeout_ms), i.e. every queued write waits its full timeout and is dropped.

The engine is serving reads but cannot persist anything: while it runs, an independent process cannot take the write lock either ('BEGIN IMMEDIATE' -> database is locked, rolled back immediately), and the newest system_health row is stuck at the boot timestamp 2026-11-13 15:29:43. Failing writes name source:dexscreener_profiles, source:dexscreener_pairs, source:geckoterminal_new_pools and source:birdeye. A write transaction opened during boot is never committed or released; nothing after boot is stored.

SIGINT does not stop the engine on this revision (reproduced on three separate instances): it logs engine_shutdown_signal, keeps failing health inserts and stays up past 60s, so SIGKILL is the only working stop. The finish.sh amendment uses SIGKILL.

Gate requires the root .env to be set aside: test_api_fail_closed_when_token_unset expects 403, but common/config.py reads env_file='.env' and the local token makes it 401. finish.sh moved .env aside and restored it; the sha256 before/after comparison passed.
GitHub Actions on origin/main was already red before this task: 'Archive and parity' failed on f44ddbd across the 2026-11-10, 11-11 and 11-12 scheduled runs.
how_to_stop: kill -KILL $(cat ~/serpent-logs/engine.pid)  (SIGINT wedges; the process may leave an orphan Streamlit on 8501 - check with ss -ltn and kill it too)
